body:
You are drafting short lines of game text for a single-player D&D 2024 computer RPG set in Curse of Strahd's Barovia. Reply in plain text only. Do not message, route to, or ask anyone else; finish with your reply.

HOUSE RULES FOR ALL LINES
- ALLUDE, NEVER QUOTE. This game winks at another famous fantasy game in small ways, but no line may contain a name, quote, or phrase from another game, and no line may mention a game, a player, dice, rolls, levels or saving. Everything happens inside the world.
- Do not use these words at all: tadpole, illithid, mind flayer, nautiloid, squid-ship.
- The tone is gothic, dry and quietly funny, never cruel.
- Give TWO options for every line so the editor can choose. Label each option A or B.
- Format every spoken line as: Speaker [mood]: Text   (mood optional; one of neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly). One or two sentences a line.

THE SPEAKERS: three Vistani women at the corner table of the Blood of the Vine, the tavern in the Village of Barovia. They speak as a trio.
- Alenka (eldest, leader): honeyed and theatrical, speaks for the three. Real lines: "Sit, strangers. New faces in Barovia! That happens about as often as sunshine. Buy us a cup and tell us everything." / "Vistani. Our wagons go where they like; the mists open for us."
- Mirabel (middle): mocking, quick, laughs at everyone, including herself. Real lines: "Or don't. We'll guess. Our guesses are always better than the truth." / "Ismark the Lesser. His father was loud, and brave, and dead. Ismark is quiet, and brave, and not dead yet. Give him time." / "Or to sell tickets."
- Sorvia (youngest): blurts true things, then gets elbowed. Real lines: "Your boots have walked farther than boots should, in this valley. Sorry. I notice things." / "She's nice. She mended my horse's bridle once and wouldn't take a copper. I hope... nothing. More wine?"
Shared: "our people", "the mists", "the cards". Never modern slang.

THE SCENE: the party asks the sisters, "Seen any other strangers come through?" The mists of Barovia sometimes swallow travellers from other lands. The sisters tell, laughing, about a man the mists brought last spring: he came stumbling out of a field, singed, swearing that a great flying ship, shaped like a squid and as big as a church, had fallen out of the sky with him aboard; and he swore a worm had crawled into his head through his eye and was whispering to him. Mirabel says it was a stye. Sorvia felt sorry for him and gave him a bread roll. He walked off east toward Vallaki and they never saw him again. The man is NEVER named. Light, gossipy, funny; it is just a tavern story.

WRITE (a short exchange, 4 to 6 lines in all, in this order of beats):
1. Alenka begins the story (the field, the singed stranger, the flying ship like a squid). One or two sentences.
2. Mirabel adds the worm in the eye, mocking. One or two sentences.
3. Sorvia's soft truth (she gave him bread; or she noticed something odd about his eye).
4. Mirabel or Alenka: it was a stye.
5. Alenka closes: he walked east; the mists bring all sorts.

Return exactly this layout:
1A: Alenka ...: ...
1B: Alenka ...: ...
2A: Mirabel ...: ...
2B: Mirabel ...: ...
3A: Sorvia ...: ...
3B: Sorvia ...: ...
4A: ...
4B: ...
5A: Alenka ...: ...
5B: Alenka ...: ...
result:
1A: Alenka [smile]: Last spring, a man came stumbling out of a turnip field with his eyebrows singed right off. He swore on his mother's bones that a flying vessel shaped like a monstrous cuttlefish, big as a church, had tumbled out of the heavens with him aboard.
1B: Alenka [sly]: Only last spring, the mists spat a fellow into the wet grass outside the village, still smoking at the boots. He raved to anyone with ears that a great sky-galleon with tentacles like a squid and a hull the size of a cathedral had crashed through the clouds.
2A: Mirabel [sly]: Better still, he claimed a wriggling little maggot had burrowed straight through his eye and taken up residence behind his forehead. Said it was whispering secrets to him, though it didn't tell him where to find a decent pair of trousers.
2B: Mirabel [smile]: Oh, and that wasn't the half of it—he clutched his head and insisted a tiny worm had crawled in through his eye to mutter in his ear. Strange sort of tenant, if you ask me, and paying no rent at all.
3A: Sorvia [sad]: I felt sorry for him and gave him a warm crust of bread from my apron. His left eye really did twitch in the oddest way when he thanked me, almost as if something inside were looking back.
3B: Sorvia [neutral]: He looked half-starved, so I slipped him a heel of dark bread before he went on his way. I looked right at his eye when he took it, and the pupil was all clouded and shivering... sorry, I shouldn't stare.
4A: Mirabel [smile]: It was a stye, little sister, and a touch of marsh fever. Men will invent a whole fleet of flying sea-monsters before they admit they rubbed their eyes with dirty fingers.
4B: Alenka [sly]: Hush now, it was nothing more than an ugly stye and too much cheap wine on an empty stomach. Stop looking so haunted, Sorvia, or you'll have our guests checking their own eyelids.
5A: Alenka [neutral]: He wandered off east toward Vallaki, still arguing with his own skull, and we never saw him again. The mists bring all sorts to this valley, though rarely with such lively imaginations.
5B: Alenka [smile]: Once he ate Sorvia's bread, he marched straight down the east road toward Vallaki and vanished into the pines. Our mists are terrible thieves, strangers, and they have very strange taste in what they steal.
